title: Inhibrx’s OX40 agonist add-on beats Keytruda alone in head and neck cancer
snippet: Inhibrx CEO Mark Lappe was particularly keen on INBRX-106’s performance in patients with HPV-positive disease and sees a nearly $4 billion near-term opportunity thanks to the Phase 2 results.

title: Structure’s obesity portfolio impresses on GLP-1 and amylin fronts in dual data drop
snippet: Structure Therapeutics’ oral GLP-1 candidate aleniglipron showed 72-week efficacy “in line” with Novo Nordisk’s oral Wegovy, BMO Capital Markets wrote in a note to investors. Meanwhile, Structure’s amylin and calcitonin receptor agonist ACCG-2671 showed “impressive” target engagement in a Phase 1 trial of healthy volu...

title: Novo shutters 2 more heart disease studies, indicating IL-6 is ‘invalid target’
snippet: After the failure of Novo Nordisk’s IL-6 inhibitor ziltivekimab sent waves through the industry, the company has terminated two other studies of the asset, bringing the total number of high-profile cardiovascular flops to six over nine weeks.

title: Roivant's pulmonary hypertension drug shines with ‘blowout’ Phase 2 data
snippet: Mosliciguat, being developed by the Roivant Sciences subsidiary Pulmovant, 'significantly exceeded expectations' in reducing pulmonary vascular resistance, according to analysts, and is progressing to a late-stage study.

title: AstraZeneca’s SERD pill overcomes adcomm defeat to win FDA nod in breast cancer
snippet: The approval opens up a “modest” market for AstraZeneca’s Etcamah, according to Leerink analysts, who nevertheless looked forward to an upcoming late-stage readout that could lead to a “significantly larger opportunity” for the drug.

title: Novartis’ $12B Avidity acquisition hits Phase 3 speedbump as dystrophy drug disappoints
snippet: While Novartis’ antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate failed to significantly improve hand function in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1, the asset nevertheless showed signs of clinical activity in secondary and exploratory measures.

title: Moonwalk pulls in $70M to take fat-targeting RNAi obesity candidate to clinic
snippet: Moonwalk Biosciences plans to shepherd its lead obesity asset into first-in-human trials in late 2027. In preclinical studies, MW101 has demonstrated weight loss and fat reduction while maintaining muscle mass.

title: Novartis’ cholesterol-lowering medicine fails Phase 3, clouding Lp(a) horizons
snippet: The failure of Novartis’ pelacarsen to translate its Lp(a)-lowering effects to clinical benefits “marks a meaningful setback” for other companies taking a similar approach to cardiovascular risk, analysts say—including Eli Lilly and Amgen.

title: BrainChild Bio targets deadly pediatric brain cancer with $116M series A
snippet: BrainChild Bio’s lead asset BCB-276 is in pivotal development for diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, a rare and fatal brain tumor that affects around 300 children in the U.S. every year.

title: Can Benelux turn scientific strength into larger biotech scale?
snippet: Belgium and the Netherlands have built some of Europe's strongest life sciences ecosystems, powered by leading research institutions and a growing pool of experienced biotech talent. While early-stage funding remains scarce and investment is often fragmented across regions, investors see national biotech initiatives a...

title: AI will only revolutionize drug discovery and development if we play to its strengths
snippet: Foundation models will change the way we study the natural, applied and clinical sciences, but only under certain conditions, and not in the way that some AI leaders claim.

title: 4 CDMOs to consider when outsourcing manufacturing
snippet: Contract development and manufacturing organizations looking to do business with biopharmas include Lonza, which has more than 30 sites, and Samsung Biologics, which recently announced a planned acquisition of another CDMO.

title: Moderna and Merck’s mRNA success fuels focus on ‘scaling out and scaling down’
snippet: After mastering mass-market mRNA production during the pandemic, the industry now needs to achieve the timely delivery of individualized vaccines to thousands of patients.

title: Reeling from past failures, Parkinson's pipeline enters 'era of diversification'
snippet: While some drugmakers continue to walk the alpha-synuclein antibody path, others like AC Immune opt for new approaches that could bring the first-ever disease-modifying therapy for Parkinson's disease.

title: TScan axes 75% of workforce, prioritizes solid tumor program
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: 10 life sciences startups selected for accelerator program
snippet: Seven of the 10 companies participating in the fall cohorts of MassBio and SCbio’s Drive program are based in the United States, including four in Massachusetts.

title: Biotech is back, with H1 progress smoothing glide path through end of year: Truist
snippet: With M&A rising, venture capital returning and policy risks easing, biotech is on a positive trajectory following a prolonged post-pandemic slump, Truist Securities declared after a survey of sector leaders.

title: Pfizer punts Seagen ADC, further muddying value of the $43B buyout
snippet: The co-development deal comes after Pfizer reported a late-stage failure for a Seagen asset and the discontinuation of another investigational therapy developed by the company as a subsidiary of the pharma.

title: AbbVie’s T cell engager delivers survival benefit in Phase 3 multiple myeloma study
snippet: AbbVie’s etentamig has a relatively cleaner safety profile and an administration schedule that could give it an edge over other BCMA-targeting multiple myeloma therapies on the market, according to BMO Capital Markets.

title: FDA approves Ionis’ antisense drug as first targeted therapy for Alexander disease
snippet: Zanvastro, an antisense oligonucleotide therapy, represents the first independent neurology launch for Ionis Pharmaceuticals, which intends to leverage the foothold for more approvals in rare neurodegenerative diseases, including Angelman syndrome.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?
